newsitem.title: USA: Republic sees EPS before charges in-line.
newsitem.headline: Republic sees EPS before charges in-line.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc said Tuesday that fourth quarter and full-year earnings excluding Alamo Rent-A-Car results and extraordinary charges should be in-line with analysts estimates.
The charges will include about $30 million net of taxes for refinancing Alamo debt, including the completed tender offer of Alamo senior notes due 2006.

In addition, Republic said it will also take a one-time pretax charge of abuot $90 million in the fourth quarter for integrating the operations of Alamo, which it agreed to buy in November in a pact valued then at about $625 million.
Excluding Alamo's results and these charges, Republic should meet First Call estimates of $0.06 per share for the quarter, company spokesman Michael Karsner said.
Wall Street puts the company's fiscal 1996 earnings at $0.26 per share, according to First Call consensus estimates.

Republic said additionally that it is also "currently comfortable with analysts expectations for full year 1997," which Karsner said are expected at $0.55 per share excluding Alamo's results and extraordinary charges.
The company said it would report fourth quarter results at the end of January.
Republic shares were off 1/8 Tuesday morning at 30-3/4.
